newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Choppy dlr/yen suggests top near 120.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Choppy dlr/yen suggests top near 120.

text.p: Choppy consolidation in dollar/yen since last week's high suggests the conclusion of the latest uptrend may be at hand, forex analysts said.
After sliding from Friday's peak at 120.15, dollar/yen has rattled around in a 118.30 to 119.70 range. Chartists said this activity is a typical feature of topping patterns.

"The price action has been quite narrow," said Ben Morden, technical analyst at I.D.E.A. Inc. "This uncertainty is kind of characteristic near tops, where you have a bit of volatility and some sideways price action before tops."
Darren Spain, global foreign exchange analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston, agreed, saying he was becoming "wary" of a pullback from just over the 120 yen level.
At 1300 EST on Monday, dollar/yen was trading at 119.55/65 up from its 119.24/29 U.S. open.
However, analysts allowed for some leeway, saying the dollar may push higher again yet still leave the top in place.
After reaching an objective near such a key psychological level, Morden said he would tolerate another move above 120.15 yen, to 120.50, before shifting focus to new upside targets.
Spain placed the threshold somewhat higher.
"I don't necessarily anticipate a break of 120.75. I'm on reversal watch," he said. "You have that resistance band at 120.00 to 120.35, where we expect that reversal from."
If the 120.50 to 120.75 yen area is exceeded, analysts target a quick move to 122.25/50, citing a lack of impediments from chartpoints in between.
But if the dollar closes below 118.30 yen on a daily basis, a test of 117.40 should ensue, analysts said.
Below there, rising trendline support drawn off the December 6 low at 111.73 yen comes in at 116.65 on Monday, analysts said.
In dollar/mark, Monday's push to a new 31-month high at 1.6493 puts the bullish big picture back in focus, analysts said.
To restore the uptrend, a close above last week's 31-month high at 1.6455 is needed, they said. A break above 1.65 marks would target 1.6665.
"But if we do close today back below 1.6440 marks, then this would look like just some sort of squeeze," said Ture Johnson, technical analyst at Bank of America.
At 1300 EST, dollar/mark was trading at 1.6480/90, up from 1.6365/75 at the open. ((--Alden Bentley, 212 859 1667))
